title: Mayo Clinic credits AI with finding a woman's ruptured brain aneurysm in minutes before her emergency treatment and recovery
summary: Mayo Clinic says that AI algorithms, which no source names, let its care team find Sophia Chan's ruptured aneurysm in minutes; she had surgery and recovered.
account: On 24 February 2022, Sophia Chan became unresponsive after an aneurysm ruptured. Her care team at Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, located the aneurysm within minutes. She underwent surgery, although her husband was initially told that she was unlikely to survive. After weeks of stabilization, she recovered. She spent 24 days in the hospital. On 28 October 2022 Mayo Clinic News Network reported the date of the stroke and the length of her stay. That account does not mention AI. On 13 January 2025 Mayo Clinic Magazine reported that AI algorithms had allowed the care team to find her aneurysm in minutes. The magazine also reported that, two years after the stroke, she had resumed an active family life and was taking part in the DISCOVERY study of post-stroke cognitive impairment. No source names the software or compares her care with care without it.
system: AI analysis of brain CT images

ratings.reason: Chan survived a critical hemorrhage and regained an active life. Mayo credits AI with aiding diagnosis.

ai_role.statement: Mayo Clinic Magazine says that AI algorithms let the care team find the aneurysm in minutes. It calls those algorithms and her short distance from the hospital likely keys to her recovery. Her care team operated and treated her for almost three weeks before her condition was stable. No source names the software or compares her care with care without it. Mayo's October 2022 account of the case does not mention AI.

brief: Sophia Chan's recovery at Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida, is a story that Mayo tells about its use of AI in stroke care. Her brain aneurysm ruptured on 24 February 2022, and her husband was told at first that she was unlikely to survive. She spent 24 days in the hospital, and Mayo reports that two years after the stroke she was getting back to an active family life. Mayo's account of 28 October 2022 does not mention AI.[1] On 13 January 2025, Mayo Clinic Magazine credited AI algorithms with letting the care team find her aneurysm in minutes, and it named her short distance from the hospital as another likely key to her recovery.[2] No source names the software or compares her care with care without it.
